messages:
maria_support: Hi all, opening thread — customer reports intermittent 10s socket timeouts to hosted API from their on-prem Private deployment. App logs show curl (28) and occasional 407 from corp proxy.
customer_ops: Confirmed. Services in our onprem cluster hit api.redwood.com and fail. Other external hosts (github.com) work through the proxy. We run an egress gateway -> corp-proxy (NTLM) chain.
eng_oncall_jake: Can you run quick checks from a failing pod/host and paste outputs? curl -v --proxy http://corp-proxy:8080 https://api.redwood.com/health ; dig +short api.redwood.com ; traceroute -n api.redwood.com ; openssl s_client -connect <ip>:443 -servername api.redwood.com
customer_ops: curl via proxy returns HTTP/1.1 407 Proxy Authentication Required (NTLM). Direct curl without proxy times out connecting to resolved IP.
devops_amit: Sounds like (A) proxy auth not handled by apps and (B) direct egress blocked by firewall or appliance. If your gateway must reach corp-proxy, it should either perform NTLM auth or present credentials to pods.
customer_ops: We're seeing TLS inspection on the path (corporate MITM). Browsers get corp CA cert. Our runtime fails signature checks for redwood calls. Is adding the corp CA to container CA bundle acceptable?
network_eng_li: Adding corp CA to the app truststore is the normal enterprise workaround. Safer: request TLS passthrough for api.redwood.com in the inspection appliance or add an inspection bypass for that FQDN so the original cert is preserved.
customer_ops: We tried adding corp CA and still hit 407s. Logs show firewall drops to public IPs for api.redwood.com. infra_bot: firewall log: dropped outbound tcp to 34.120.45.67:443 from 10.3.5.12 rule=egress-deny-1001
maria_support: Two remediation options: (1) Allowlist Redwood IPs/hostnames and permit CONNECT without interception; (2) Gateways should NTLM-auth to corp-proxy on behalf of pods and do TLS passthrough to avoid MITM.
devops_amit: Example gateway pattern — run a small proxy on gateway that authenticates to corp-proxy (cntlm or squid with cache_peer). Sample squid snippet:
```
cache_peer corp-proxy.domain parent 8080 0 no-query default login=PASS
acl redwood dstdomain .api.redwood.com
cache_peer_access corp-proxy allow redwood
```
And iptables NAT on gateway:
```
iptables -t nat -A POSTROUTING -s 10.3.0.0/16 -o eth0 -j MASQUERADE
```
customer_ops: If we must keep inspection, can we restrict corp CA to only our redwood flows? We don't want to trust it globally.
eng_oncall_jake: You can bake a special image that includes the corp CA for only services that call external APIs. Or mount a custom CA bundle into containers via secret. Also confirm DNS — split-horizon could be returning internal mirror IPs.
customer_ops: Good catch — our split DNS resolves api.redwood.com to an internal mirror leftover. That mirror is offline and times out. We're flipping the A record to public IPs now.
customer_ops: Attaching tcpdump (trimmed) of failed connect: "12:34:56.789 IP 10.3.5.12.54321 > 34.120.45.67.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460], length 0" then no SYN-ACK.
maria_support: That confirms SYN dropped or blocked upstream. Once you switch DNS or allowlist IPs we can test again. Also please capture the proxy logs showing 407 responses and timestamp of the tcpdump.
customer_ops: We'll try the gateway+cntlm approach and update. Thanks, will ping when we have proxy logs and tcpdump.
maria_support: Thanks — we'll standby. If you want us to share Redwood IP ranges for allowlisting, call out and we'll provide. Tag @eng_oncall_jake when you add logs.
eng_oncall_jake: Quick tip — when using curl with NTLM through a proxy: curl --proxy-user 'DOMAIN\\user:pass' --proxy-ntlm --proxy http://corp-proxy:8080 https://api.redwood.com/health
customer_ops: Trying that now — curl with --proxy-ntlm returns 200 OK to /health when run from gateway box (after cntlm). From pods still timing out until DNS is fixed. Will follow up.
infra_bot: thread state=open
maria_support: Leaving thread open until confirmed resolved. :thumbsup:
